GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; its initial x-y is a starting location that may remain or change by one rigid translation. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
DIAGNOSTIC OCCUPANCY: LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE. Occupancy does not change placement permission. For every camera view, keep the product at its initial x-y or use one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation for a usable composition. Preserve exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never resize, reorient, reproject, redraw, crop, or occlude the product. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together.

Move the printer horizontally right by one printer width, with no vertical movement, using one rigid image-plane translation. This places it right of center and frees the left side for sorting and circulation, rather than merely increasing prominence. Independently build a pale oak output table beneath it, extending about one printer width to its left and half a printer width to its right. Fully support the base, with a modest strip of tabletop in front and generous side clearance. The printer’s back and the table’s back edge stand directly against the wall. Keep the near-side standing approach and the left-hand circulation area clear. Replace all baseline support geometry with furniture aligned to the unchanged printer.

Camera: Use the unchanged moderately wide view, from below standing eye level and gently looking down, with a level horizon and no camera roll. Preserve the printer’s visible front, narrow left side and top exactly. The table’s long edges rise gently toward image right, while its depth edges recede toward the upper left, sharing the printer’s chassis directions. Construct the wall and floor around that perspective without changing the product’s projection. The right-of-center printer remains its original pixel size, fully supported against the wall with an unobstructed approach from the foreground.

Composition: The printer occupies the middle plane right of center, retaining its exact view and dimensions after the single horizontal translation. A pale oak table supports its entire base with natural contact shadow, clear side margins and a short front working ledge. Its back edge and the printer’s back meet the wall directly, without intervening objects. The table’s left portion provides a sorting surface; a small stack of blank white paper rests at its far-left end in the middle plane, beside rather than in front of the printer. Keep most of that surface empty. A dusty blue matte-painted wall spans the far plane from center to right, forming a broad visible area above and beside the station. The far-left wall is warm white; light gray flooring fills the clear foreground and left circulation area. Soft clear daylight enters from the left, with generous neutral fill. No requested object or requirement needs to be omitted. Standing access serves the printer; no dedicated chair or invented keyboard is added.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
For every camera view, including close/high-fill views, keep the product at its initial location or reposition it using only one rigid image-plane x-y translation when that improves usable composition. This changes position only, not the product view or size.

Preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead.

The only permitted product change is one rigid image-plane x-y translation. Keep its exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, perspective, projection, foreshortening, silhouette, aspect proportions, open/closed and powered state, finish, details, logo and display content. Do not rotate, mirror, resize, shear, warp, reproject, redraw or activate the product. Do not zoom, reframe or change the viewpoint in a way that alters the product.

At the chosen product position, compose a category- and scenario-appropriate support beneath its weight-bearing base. The support may change independently of the product's translation: do not preserve baseline product-to-edge distances, support top extents or absolute support-edge locations as requirements. Fully support the base without floating or overhang, with believable front, back and side clearances, natural weight-bearing contact, a contact shadow and material-appropriate reflections on the support.

Construct furniture around the unchanged product orientation. A printer must sit square to its support in 3D with usable access to its operating front. A printer must face a usable seating or working edge with clear access to its keyboard and display. Do not rotate the product or reveal a different face to fit the furniture. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.

GUIDE LEGEND: Image 1 is the current canvas to edit. Its real product pixels establish the exact product appearance, view and pixel size to preserve. Their frame position may remain unchanged or change by one rigid x-y translation. The flat gray region and its boundaries show an initial support plan, not output pixels or required support edges, distances or extents. At the chosen product position, compose an appropriate support beneath the unchanged product. Remove all gray-guide and diagram remnants, any duplicate product and any product-shaped remnant at the initial location. Keep only one intact product at the final location. Render the lighting, palette, materials and textures described here photographically. When blue is unspecified, include one large blue surface/furnishing or multiple clearly visible blue elements whose combined area makes blue immediately noticeable, not a token accent. Tiny props, thin partition frames, screen graphics, sky and lighting casts alone do not qualify. Keep the planned blue materials, visible extent and placement consistent; leave small props neutral by default. Explicit minimal-blue or no-blue requests override that default, as do explicit blue amounts or carriers. Keep the product's original color, finish, exact orientation/view, scale, details and full visibility. Every camera view permits only one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation. Never change the product or its camera viewpoint to make room for blue. Retain requested warm-neutral lighting alongside physical blue materials. Do not impose a universal blue hue or coverage percentage. Match soft, uniform exposure and gentle contrast; no bright-hero/dark-room treatment and no orange or global blue color cast. The product pixels in Image 1 control all product details, including any unlit display. Never reproduce any diagram lines, boxes, labels, text or flat guide colors.

Turn Image 1 into a photograph; preserve the printer's exact orientation/view, pixel size and details; only its x-y position may change. Never mirror, shear, warp, redraw, activate or occlude it.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other invariant; never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible; where translation is allowed, retain initial x-y if a move cannot preserve every invariant.

Independently construct a pale oak output table beneath it, square to its chassis, extending about one printer width left and half a width right, with full base support, side clearances, a modest front ledge and natural contact shadow. The printer's back stands right against the wall at the support's back edge, with no gap, shelf or objects between them. Leave unobstructed standing access in front. Place blank white paper at the table's far-left end, beside the printer.

Use a moderately wide, gently downward view without roll; match furniture and room perspective to the fixed printer. A dusty blue matte-painted wall spans the far plane from center to right, forming a broad visible area above and beside the station. Keep warm-white walls left and light-gray floor circulation clear. Soft clear daylight from the left, generous fill, gentle contrast, visible oak grain; no people. Remove guides, old shadows and ghosts; complete the vacated location, leaving exactly one fully visible printer.

One full-bleed photorealistic photograph with natural imperfections; no added text, logos, borders, watermark or CGI look.

Every camera view permits only one rigid x-y translation. The support is recomposed beneath the product's chosen position with believable edge clearances, access, full base contact and a plausible contact shadow. The surrounding scene has consistent perspective. The product is fully visible and unoccluded. No product distortion is allowed.
